summary.text: A 34-year-old Chinese woman presented to the clinic with progressive right-sided vertigo and hearing loss. Two days after an upper respiratory tract infection she developed right ear fullness, low-frequency tinnitus and vertigo after vigorous nose blowing. She denied fever, otalgia, headache, otorrhea, nausea and vomiting and had no history of ear disease, ear surgery, recent head trauma or chronic systemic disorders. Examination showed nasal congestion with purulent discharge, a right bulging hyperemic tympanic membrane and slight right-beating horizontal spontaneous nystagmus.

Right ear audiometry showed mixed hearing loss (air-bone gap 24 dB HL) with normal left hearing, and tympanometry was type B on the right and type A on the left. Videonystagmography showed right-beating horizontal and upbeat positional nystagmus, and vHIT showed a VOR gain of 0.45 without corrective saccades. CT showed increased density in the right mastoid air cells, MRI showed right mastoid T1 low and T2 high signal, and endoscopy showed right middle ear fluid. Right horizontal semicircular canal hypointense cupula was diagnosed.

The patient received intravenous ceftriaxone sodium 2 g and dexamethasone 10 mg once daily for 5 days with hydroxymethazoline and mometasone furoate nasal sprays. A planned tympanic membrane incision was cancelled because symptoms improved significantly the following day. Ear fullness, hearing impairment and dizziness improved within 24 hours of treatment initiation.

Within a week audiometric thresholds returned to normal, nystagmus intensity diminished and vertigo resolved. Middle ear fluid had resolved on endoscopy on 28 July 2024, vHIT gain was normalized in all canals on 29 July 2024, and audiometry and tympanometry were normal on 8 August 2024. Serial audiological monitoring was performed. The patient reported satisfaction with treatment, but residual high-frequency tinnitus persisted and she was diagnosed with persistent high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss.

ambiguities.issue: The text attributes the reduced vHIT gain of 0.45 to the anterior semicircular canal, whereas the Fig. 4 caption names the affected posterior semicircular canal. The printed Fig. 4 panel A labels the 0.45 gain as R anterior; pixel readings are not recorded as facts.

evidence.quote: diminished vestibulo–ocular reflex (VOR) gain of 0.45 in the anterior semicircular canal on the affected side
in the affected posterior semicircular canal without corrective saccades

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not resolve which canal is correct.

ambiguities.issue: The CT text reports increased density in the right mesotympanum, whereas the Fig. 5 caption reports unobstructed bilateral mesotympanums without middle ear effusion.

evidence.quote: increased density shadows in the right mastoid air cell and mesotympanum
showing unobstructed bilateral mesotympanums (arrows), without evidence of middle ear effusion or ossicular pathologies

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not resolve the mesotympanum finding.

ambiguities.issue: The Fig. 4 caption reports a normalized VOR gain of 0.85 in all canals after treatment, but the printed gains in the figure panel are canal-specific values and none is 0.85.

evidence.quote: B Posttreatment evaluation (29 July 2024) revealed a normalized VOR gain (0.85) in all canals

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not choose between the caption value and the printed panel values.

ambiguities.issue: The discussion states initial management included drainage procedures, whereas the case text states the planned tympanic membrane incision was cancelled and describes no drainage procedure performed. The discussion also says residual high-frequency tinnitus persisted "after the procedure" without naming any procedure.

evidence.quote: Initial therapeutic management included antibiotics, glucocorticoids, and drainage procedures.
The planned tympanic membrane incision was cancelled as the patient’s symptoms significantly improved the following day.
residual high-frequency tinnitus persisted after the procedure

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record a drainage procedure as performed.

ambiguities.issue: The case says hearing normalized within a week, but the posttreatment audiogram and tympanogram in the figure captions are dated 8 August 2024, 14 days after the 25 July 2024 initial tests, and the vHIT follow-up is dated 29 July 2024.

evidence.quote: Within 1 week, the patient’s hearing levels normalized
B Posttreatment assessment (8 August 2024) revealed complete normalization of the right ear thresholds

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer dates for treatment start or for when normalization occurred.

ambiguities.issue: The bedside ocular motor examination is reported as normal smooth pursuit, whereas videonystagmography reports type II smooth pursuit (called impairment in the Fig. 3 caption).

evidence.quote: Ocular motor tests revealed normal saccadic eye movements and smooth pursuit
smooth pursuit was type II

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not reconcile the bedside and videonystagmography smooth pursuit results.

ambiguities.issue: The source says the patient was intolerant and unable to cooperate with the caloric test before treatment, but does not state whether the test was started, abandoned or not performed, and gives no result.

ambiguities.issue: Hearing is reported as normalized (text: within a week; Fig. 1 caption: complete normalization of right ear thresholds on 8 August 2024), yet the discussion states she was diagnosed with persistent high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, at an unstated time.

evidence.quote: revealed complete normalization of the right ear thresholds
She was diagnosed with persistent high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not date the high-frequency hearing loss diagnosis or resolve it against the normalization statements.

ambiguities.issue: The Fig. 3 caption reports resolution of spontaneous nystagmus and mild residual positional nystagmus after treatment, while the text says horizontal nystagmus gradually abated and upbeat nystagmus resolved completely.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the seven figure JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual submission.
Text and Fig. 4 caption disagree on whether the reduced vHIT gain of 0.45 is in the anterior or posterior semicircular canal; both kept as review-only facts.
Text reports increased density in the right mesotympanum on CT, while the Fig. 5 caption reports unobstructed bilateral mesotympanums without middle ear effusion; both kept as review-only facts.
Fig. 4 caption states a normalized VOR gain of 0.85 in all canals after treatment, which is not among the canal-specific gains printed in the panel.
Discussion mentions drainage procedures that the case text does not describe; no drainage procedure is recorded as performed.

Discussion statements that CT and MRI were performed in all patients and the mechanistic hypotheses (hypointense cupula, round window membrane pathway, superior vestibular nerve) are author interpretation or cohort wording and are not recorded as patient facts, except the stated diagnosis of right horizontal semicircular canal hypointense cupula.
Test dates come only from figure caption sentences; the case text gives no dates, and the treatment start date is not stated.
Fig. 3 caption states resolution of spontaneous nystagmus after treatment while the text states horizontal nystagmus gradually abated; kept without reconciliation.
Fig. 5 caption calls panels B and C coronal sections, whereas the slices look axial in the pixels; recorded in the visual review only.
